bob-build-on-bitcoin.upside: A real Bitcoin layer-2 with Coinbase, Kraken and KuCoin listings and code pushed this week; the only possible lift is renewed interest in Bitcoin DeFi, with no dated event.
bob-build-on-bitcoin.cheap: Down 87% since its December 2025 launch, and only 48% of tokens are out, so steady unlocks keep selling pressure on it.
bob-build-on-bitcoin.wrongIf: Trading falls back under $2M a day within a week, or no project news by mid-December.
bob-build-on-bitcoin.vsScanner: The 15.5x trading spike has no news behind it that I can find; the score jump comes from the spike, not from anything new.

skale.upside: An existing gas-free chain with ongoing work; no dated catalyst found.
skale.cheap: Down 99.7% from its 2021 high; not mispriced, just out of favour.
skale.wrongIf: Trading under $3M a day, or the price makes a new low under $0.0028.
skale.vsScanner: The 'new Gemini listing' that brought it back is old: Gemini listed SKL in March 2021. That is not a catalyst.

kyve-network.upside: A data-validation chain backed by known funds; I found no dated event to explain the 77% weekly jump.
kyve-network.cheap: At a $3.5M value with only $80K traded a day, almost nobody is watching it.
kyve-network.wrongIf: The weekly gain reverses within 7 days, or daily trading stays under $100K.
kyve-network.vsScanner: The scanner likes the weekly move, but it happened on very thin trading, so it can reverse just as easily.

theoriq.upside: Its 2026 plans promised staking and opening the platform to outside builders in the second half of the year; I found nothing showing either has shipped.
theoriq.cheap: It fell 95% from its December 2025 high, and it has shown no activity in months, so people have stopped paying attention.
theoriq.wrongIf: No shipped product news by the end of December 2026.
theoriq.vsScanner: I agree with the scanner's zombie flag; the Coinbase and Bithumb listings are the only thing that keeps it alive.

nextplace.upside: It now runs a working quantum-computing marketplace (OpenQuantum) with a paid tier and a university research tie-up; no dated launch is ahead.
nextplace.cheap: It trades only inside the Bittensor subnet market, and the Bittensor sector is falling, so few outside buyers can reach it.
nextplace.wrongIf: Subnet trading drops back under $150K a day, or the paid tier shows no users by January.
nextplace.vsScanner: The product is more real than most coins on today's list, but the 8.7x trading spike has no news behind it.

debox.upside: A working social app that kept announcing partnerships through April 2026; nothing is dated ahead.
debox.cheap: Trading is thin ($130K a day) and the top 10 wallets reportedly hold most of the supply.
debox.wrongIf: The price breaks below $0.015, or trading stays under $100K a day.
debox.vsScanner: The top-10 wallet concentration (89% in a 2025 report) is a red flag that the scanner doesn't show.

ethereum-classic.upside: Its block reward was cut in August 2026 and treasury voting is being tested, but there is no dated event ahead.
ethereum-classic.cheap: It is a large, old coin that moves with the market; it isn't mispriced, just tied to the market's direction.
ethereum-classic.wrongIf: It loses the $5.50 area, or Bitcoin's share of the market goes above 60%.
ethereum-classic.vsScanner: Agree with the scanner's low score.

hydradx.upside: A working Polkadot exchange that cut its maximum supply to 6.5B and runs buybacks; no dated launch found.
hydradx.cheap: It trades only on its own exchange, so outside buyers can't easily get in.
hydradx.wrongIf: Daily trading stays under $50K, or Polkadot money keeps leaving.
hydradx.vsScanner: Agree with the scanner's warning about thin trading.

worldcoin-wld.upside: A real product (over 18 million people verified, plus Tinder, Zoom and DocuSign deals); no dated catalyst ahead.
worldcoin-wld.cheap: Only 38% of tokens are out and about 2.9M new tokens come out every day, so supply grows and the price keeps getting diluted.
worldcoin-wld.wrongIf: The price falls under its May 2026 low of $0.231.
worldcoin-wld.vsScanner: Agree with the scanner's low score; the product is real, but the token keeps getting diluted.

sectorNews.AI: Most AI tokens fell this week, and the sector shrank by about 7% in a risk-off market. Bittensor subnet tokens followed TAO lower. That hurts the small AI coins on today's list (JAGENT, Theoriq, Quantum Compute, InfiniteHash).
sectorNews.DeFi: There was no big DeFi news this week; crypto indexes traded lower across the board. Small DeFi tokens that only trade on their own exchange (Hydration, H2O) get no help from that.
sectorNews.Gaming: One weekly recap had gaming as the best sector by valuation change, but I couldn't confirm the date, and none of today's gaming coins (SKALE, AVC, Star Atlas) has news of its own.
sectorNews.Social: I found no SocialFi news this week. The sector is still down 90–99% from its creator-coin peaks, and that hurts DeBox, Common and Cratos.
sectorNews.Governance: I found no governance-token news this week. Worldcoin is still being diluted by new supply, and the other governance coins on the list (Cratos, Star Atlas) are near-dead.
sectorNews.Infrastructure: Fear is back, and Bitcoin's share of the market is near 60%, which means money is moving out of altcoins. Old chains (ETC, SKALE, KYVE, BOB) are moving with the market and have no news of their own.
